senses.en: to accept that something is true
to think or suppose

ex.en: I can't believe how fast this summer went by.
ex.zh: 真不敢相信這個暑假過得這麼快。

senses.en: to make someone or something seem unimportant

ex.en: Good coaches never belittle players for making mistakes.
ex.zh: 好的教練從不因球員犯錯而貶低他們。

senses.en: a beautiful woman, especially the most beautiful at an event
senses.zh: 美女；（場合中）最美的女子

ex.en: In her red gown, she was the belle of the ball.
ex.zh: 穿著紅色禮服的她是舞會上最美的女子。

senses.en: eager to fight or argue; aggressive

ex.en: The leader's bellicose speech worried neighboring countries.
ex.zh: 那位領導人好戰的演說讓鄰國感到憂心。

root.note: 傾向戰爭的 → 好戰的

senses.en: hostile and aggressive
engaged in a war
a nation or person engaged in war or conflict

ex.en: The belligerent customer shouted at the cashier.
ex.zh: 那位充滿敵意的顧客對著收銀員大吼。

root.note: 進行戰爭的 → 好鬥的

senses.en: to express sadness or complaint about something

ex.en: Many teachers bemoan the lack of funding for the arts.
ex.zh: 許多老師抱怨藝術教育的經費不足。

senses.en: a prayer asking for God's blessing, especially at the end of a service

ex.en: The priest ended the ceremony with a benediction.
ex.zh: 神父以祝禱結束了儀式。

senses.en: a church position that provides a priest with income or property

ex.en: The young priest was given a small benefice in a country parish.
ex.zh: 那位年輕神父獲派到鄉下教區擔任一個小小的有俸聖職。

senses.en: doing good or causing good to be done; generous

ex.en: A beneficent donor paid for the new library wing.
ex.zh: 一位慈善的捐助者出資興建了圖書館的新側館。

mn: beneficent（做好事的）重點在行動；benevolent（善意的）重點在心意。

senses.en: a person who gains or benefits from something
a person who receives money or property from a will or insurance

ex.en: She was named the sole beneficiary of her uncle's will.
ex.zh: 她被指定為叔叔遺囑的唯一受益人。

root.note: 得到好處的人 → 受益者

senses.en: an advantage or helpful result
to receive help or gain an advantage; to be good for
money provided by the government or an employer

ex.en: Regular exercise has many health benefits, and everyone can benefit from it.
ex.zh: 規律運動對健康有許多好處，每個人都能從中受益。

senses.en: the quality of being kind and generous

ex.en: The old king was known for his wisdom and benevolence.
ex.zh: 那位老國王以智慧和仁慈聞名。

root.note: 懷著好的意願 → 仁慈

senses.en: kind and gracious, especially toward those of lower rank
favorable or beneficial

ex.en: The queen gave the children a benignant smile.
ex.zh: 女王對孩子們露出慈祥的微笑。

root.note: 天性善良的 → 慈祥的

senses.en: kindness and gentleness

ex.en: Her grandmother's benignity made every visitor feel welcome.
ex.zh: 她奶奶的慈祥讓每位訪客都覺得備受歡迎。

senses.en: (literary) a blessing

ex.en: The rain after the long drought felt like a benison to the farmers.
ex.zh: 久旱之後的雨，對農民來說就像一份祝福。

senses.en: to leave property to someone in a will
to pass something on to future generations

ex.en: She plans to bequeath her house to her nephew.
ex.zh: 她打算把房子遺贈給她的姪子。

root.note: （在遺囑中）說明給誰 → 遺贈

senses.en: to deprive someone of a close relative or friend through death

ex.en: The war would bereave thousands of families of their sons.
ex.zh: 這場戰爭會讓成千上萬的家庭失去兒子。

mn: 最常見形容詞 bereaved（喪親的），例如 the bereaved family。

senses.en: a bed on a ship or train
a place where a ship stays in port
to bring a ship into a berth

ex.en: I slept in the upper berth on the overnight train.
ex.zh: 我在夜車上睡上鋪。

mn: give someone a wide berth 意為「遠遠避開某人」。

senses.en: to ask someone urgently and emotionally; to beg

ex.en: I beseech you to reconsider before it is too late.
ex.zh: 我懇求你在一切太遲之前重新考慮。

senses.en: to trouble or threaten persistently
to surround or attack from all sides

ex.en: Money problems continue to beset the small company.
ex.zh: 財務問題持續困擾著這家小公司。

root.note: 四面都被放了東西 → 包圍、困擾

senses.en: to smear with something dirty or sticky
to damage someone's reputation

ex.en: Rumors could besmear the good name of an honest man.
ex.zh: 謠言可能玷汙一個誠實之人的好名聲。

senses.en: cruel or savage like a wild animal

ex.en: The prisoners suffered bestial treatment at the hands of the guards.
ex.zh: 囚犯遭到守衛野蠻的對待。

senses.en: to scatter things over a surface

ex.en: The flower girls will bestrew the aisle with rose petals.
ex.zh: 花童們會在走道上撒滿玫瑰花瓣。

senses.en: to sit or stand with one leg on each side of
to dominate or tower over

ex.en: The knight had to bestride his horse in heavy armor.
ex.zh: 騎士必須穿著笨重的盔甲跨上馬背。

senses.en: (old use) to think about or remind oneself of something

ex.en: Before you act, bethink yourself of the consequences.
ex.zh: 行動之前，先想想後果。

senses.en: (old use) to happen or happen to

ex.en: Woe betide anyone who arrives late to her class.
ex.zh: 誰上她的課遲到，誰就要倒大楣。

mn: 幾乎只用在 woe betide...（…要倒楣了）。

senses.en: (old use) early; in good time

ex.en: The farmer rose betimes to milk the cows.
ex.zh: 農夫一早就起床擠牛奶。

root.note: 在時間之內 → 及時、早

senses.en: to formally promise someone in marriage

ex.en: In the old story, the king plans to betroth his daughter to a prince.
ex.zh: 在那個古老的故事裡，國王打算把女兒許配給一位王子。

senses.en: a formal agreement to marry; an engagement

ex.en: The two families celebrated the betrothal with a large feast.
ex.zh: 兩個家族舉辦盛宴慶祝這樁婚約。

senses.en: a sloping edge or surface
to cut a sloping edge on something

ex.en: The carpenter used a plane to bevel the edge of the table.
ex.zh: 木匠用刨刀把桌緣刨成斜角。

senses.en: to confuse someone completely

ex.en: The long list of rules may bewilder new players.
ex.zh: 一長串的規則可能會讓新玩家摸不著頭緒。

senses.en: a list of books and sources used or referred to in a piece of writing

ex.en: Remember to include a bibliography at the end of your research paper.
ex.zh: 記得在研究報告最後附上參考書目。

root.note: 寫下書的清單 → 參考書目

senses.en: an extreme passion for collecting books

ex.en: His bibliomania filled every room of the house with old books.
ex.zh: 他的藏書癖讓家裡每個房間都堆滿了舊書。

root.note: 對書的狂熱 → 藏書癖

senses.en: a person who loves or collects books

ex.en: As a true bibliophile, she spends every weekend in used bookstores.
ex.zh: 身為真正的愛書人，她每個週末都泡在二手書店裡。

senses.en: fond of drinking alcohol

ex.en: The novel's bibulous uncle is always asking for another glass of wine.
ex.zh: 小說裡那位嗜酒的叔叔總是再要一杯酒。

senses.en: (old use) to remain or wait

ex.en: She decided to bide her time until the right job came along.
ex.zh: 她決定靜待時機，直到合適的工作出現。

mn: 常用片語 bide one's time，意為「靜待時機」。

senses.en: happening every two years
a plant that lives for two years; an event held every two years

ex.en: The city hosts a biennial art festival that draws visitors from abroad.
ex.zh: 這座城市每兩年舉辦一次藝術節，吸引國外遊客。

root.note: 兩年的 → 兩年一次的

mn: biennial 是兩年一次；biannual 是一年兩次。

senses.en: a stand on which a coffin or dead body is placed before burial

ex.en: The coffin rested on a bier covered with flowers.
ex.zh: 棺木停放在鋪滿鮮花的棺架上。

senses.en: a person who marries someone while already married to another

ex.en: The court discovered that the man was a bigamist with two families.
ex.zh: 法院發現這名男子是重婚者，有兩個家庭。

root.note: 有兩段婚姻的人 → 重婚者

senses.en: the crime of marrying someone while already married to another

ex.en: Bigamy is illegal in most countries.
ex.zh: 在大多數國家，重婚是違法的。

senses.en: a long, gradual curve in a coastline; a wide bay
a loop in a rope

ex.en: The fishing village sits on a sheltered bight of the coast.
ex.zh: 這座漁村位於海岸一處避風的海灣。

senses.en: involving two sides or two parties, especially two countries
affecting both sides of the body

ex.en: The two countries signed a bilateral trade agreement.
ex.zh: 兩國簽署了雙邊貿易協定。

senses.en: able to speak two languages fluently; written in two languages

ex.en: Growing up in Montreal, she became bilingual in French and English.
ex.zh: 在蒙特婁長大的她，法語和英語都說得很流利。

root.note: 兩種語言的 → 雙語的

senses.en: an early type of motion-picture projector
(rare) a short biography

ex.en: Crowds in 1900 paid a nickel to watch films on the biograph.
ex.zh: 1900 年的觀眾花五分錢，觀看用早期放映機播放的影片。

root.note: 記錄生動的畫面 → 早期電影放映機

senses.en: an account of someone's life written by another person

ex.en: I just finished reading a biography of Marie Curie.
ex.zh: 我剛讀完一本居禮夫人的傳記。

root.note: 寫下一個人的生平 → 傳記

senses.en: the scientific study of living things

ex.en: In biology class, we looked at plant cells under a microscope.
ex.zh: 在生物課上，我們用顯微鏡觀察植物細胞。

root.note: 研究生命的學問 → 生物學

senses.en: an animal that walks on two feet

ex.en: Humans are the only biped among the great apes that always walks upright.
ex.zh: 人類是大型猿類中唯一總是直立行走的兩足動物。

senses.en: a right or privilege that a person has from birth

ex.en: Many believe that a good education should be every child's birthright.
ex.zh: 許多人認為良好的教育應該是每個孩子與生俱來的權利。

senses.en: anger and resentment because of unfair treatment
a sharp, unpleasant taste

ex.en: Years later, she still felt bitterness about losing the job.
ex.zh: 多年後，她對丟掉那份工作仍然心懷怨恨。

root.note: 苦的狀態 → 苦味、怨恨

senses.en: to speak disrespectfully about God or sacred things

ex.en: In the village, it was considered a crime to blaspheme in public.
ex.zh: 在那個村子裡，公開褻瀆神明被視為犯罪。

senses.en: done openly and obviously, without shame

ex.en: Copying the whole essay from the internet was a blatant act of cheating.
ex.zh: 把整篇文章從網路上抄下來，是明目張膽的作弊行為。

senses.en: a large, strong fire
to burn brightly and strongly
a very bright display of light or color

ex.en: Firefighters worked all night to put out the blaze.
ex.zh: 消防員徹夜奮戰撲滅大火。

mn: blaze a trail 意為「開路；開創先河」。

senses.en: to display or announce something prominently
a coat of arms or its formal description

ex.en: The team will blazon its logo across every jersey and banner.
ex.zh: 球隊會把隊徽印在每件球衣和旗幟上大肆展示。

senses.en: (of a place) bare, cold, and unwelcoming
without hope or encouragement

ex.en: After the factory closed, the town's future looked bleak.
ex.zh: 工廠關閉後，這個小鎮的未來看起來一片黯淡。

senses.en: a small mark or flaw that spoils appearance
a fault in character or reputation
to spoil the appearance or quality of

ex.en: The scandal left a blemish on his otherwise spotless record.
ex.zh: 那件醜聞在他原本無瑕的紀錄上留下了一個汙點。

senses.en: showing a casual and careless lack of concern
(literary) happy and carefree

ex.en: He showed a blithe disregard for the rules.
ex.zh: 他對規則一副毫不在乎的樣子。

senses.en: (literary) cheerful and lighthearted

ex.en: The blithesome song of the birds filled the spring morning.
ex.zh: 春天的早晨充滿了鳥兒歡快的歌聲。

senses.en: the act of sealing off a place to stop goods or people from entering or leaving
to seal off a place in this way

ex.en: The navy set up a blockade to stop supplies from reaching the port.
ex.zh: 海軍實施封鎖，阻止補給運進港口。

senses.en: a ship's officer in charge of equipment and the deck crew

ex.en: The boatswain shouted orders to the sailors on deck.
ex.zh: 水手長對甲板上的水手們大聲下令。

root.note: 船上管事的人 → 水手長

mn: 拼法很長，唸法卻只有 [ˋbosṇ]，也常拼成 bosun。

senses.en: the part of a dress above the waist

ex.en: The wedding dress had a lace bodice and a long skirt.
ex.zh: 這件婚紗有蕾絲上身和長裙襬。

senses.en: relating to the body
by taking hold of the whole body; physically

ex.en: The attack caused serious bodily harm to the victim.
ex.zh: 這次攻擊對受害者造成嚴重的身體傷害。

senses.en: noisy, energetic, and cheerful

ex.en: The boisterous crowd cheered every time the home team scored.
ex.zh: 主隊每次得分，喧鬧的觀眾就歡聲雷動。

senses.en: the trunk of a tree

ex.en: The old oak had a bole so wide that four people couldn't reach around it.
ex.zh: 那棵老橡樹的樹幹粗到四個人都環抱不住。

senses.en: a Spanish dance in triple time, or music for it
a short, open jacket ending above the waist

ex.en: The orchestra played Ravel's famous bolero to close the concert.
ex.zh: 管弦樂團演奏拉威爾著名的波麗露舞曲為音樂會作結。

senses.en: the round seed pod of cotton or flax

ex.en: Each cotton boll splits open to reveal soft white fibers.
ex.zh: 每個棉鈴裂開後，就露出柔軟的白色纖維。

senses.en: a device designed to explode and cause damage
to attack with bombs
(informal) to fail badly

ex.en: Police cleared the building after a bomb threat.
ex.zh: 接到炸彈威脅後，警方疏散了整棟大樓。

senses.en: to attack continuously with bombs or shells
to direct a large number of questions or messages at someone

ex.en: Reporters began to bombard the actor with questions.
ex.zh: 記者們開始連番向那位演員提問。

root.note: 用炸彈不斷攻擊 → 砲轟

senses.en: a member of a bomber crew who aims and releases the bombs

ex.en: The bombardier waited for the signal before releasing the bombs.
ex.zh: 投彈手等到信號後才投下炸彈。

root.note: 負責砲轟的人 → 轟炸手

senses.en: high-sounding language with little meaning, used to impress

ex.en: Behind all the bombast, the politician offered no real plan.
ex.zh: 在那些浮誇的言詞背後，這位政客提不出任何實際的計畫。

root.note: 原指塞衣服的棉絮 → 塞滿空話的言詞

senses.en: rough and bad-mannered

ex.en: His boorish behavior at dinner embarrassed everyone.
ex.zh: 他在晚餐時的粗魯行為讓大家都很尷尬。

root.note: 像粗人一樣的 → 粗魯的

senses.en: to make someone feel tired and uninterested
a dull or tiresome person or thing
to make a hole with a drill

ex.en: I don't want to bore you with every detail of my trip.
ex.zh: 我不想用旅途中的每個細節讓你聽得厭煩。

senses.en: a town or district with its own local government

ex.en: Brooklyn is the most populous borough of New York City.
ex.zh: 布魯克林是紐約市人口最多的行政區。

senses.en: a woman's chest
a place of warmth, love, and protection
(of a friend) very close

ex.en: The two girls have been bosom friends since kindergarten.
ex.zh: 這兩個女孩從幼稚園起就是知心好友。

senses.en: relating to plants or the study of plants

ex.en: We saw rare orchids at the botanical garden.
ex.zh: 我們在植物園看到了稀有的蘭花。

senses.en: to study or collect plants in their natural habitat

ex.en: The students went to the mountains to botanize for their science project.
ex.zh: 學生們上山採集植物做科學專題。

senses.en: the scientific study of plants

ex.en: She studied botany and now works at a seed bank.
ex.zh: 她學植物學，現在在種子銀行工作。

senses.en: large in quantity; abundant
giving generously

ex.en: Good weather led to a bountiful harvest this year.
ex.zh: 好天氣讓今年大豐收。

root.note: 充滿豐盛的 → 豐富的

senses.en: to remove parts of a book or play considered improper or offensive

ex.en: The publisher decided to bowdlerize the novel for younger readers.
ex.zh: 出版社決定為年輕讀者刪改這部小說中不雅的部分。

root.note: 鮑德勒曾刪改莎士比亞劇作中的不雅內容 → 刪改

senses.en: a person who bowls, as in bowling or cricket
senses.zh: 打保齡球的人；（板球）投球手

senses.en: a hard black felt hat with a round top (bowler hat)

ex.en: The best bowler on our team scored over 250 points.
ex.zh: 我們隊上最厲害的保齡球選手打了超過兩百五十分。

senses.en: to refuse to buy, use, or take part in something as a protest
an act of boycotting

ex.en: Students decided to boycott the cafeteria until prices dropped.
ex.zh: 學生們決定抵制學生餐廳，直到價格調降為止。

root.note: 1880 年愛爾蘭佃農集體孤立一位叫 Boycott 的經理 → 抵制

senses.en: (Scottish) a steep hillside or slope

ex.en: Sheep grazed on the green brae above the river.
ex.zh: 羊群在河邊高處的青翠山坡上吃草。

senses.en: a person who boasts too much

ex.en: Nobody likes a braggart who talks only about his own success.
ex.zh: 沒人喜歡只會談論自己成就的吹牛大王。

senses.en: to wave something, especially a weapon, in a threatening or excited way

ex.en: The robber began to brandish a knife at the cashier.
ex.zh: 搶匪開始對著收銀員揮舞刀子。

senses.en: a bold show of confidence meant to impress or hide fear

ex.en: His bravado disappeared the moment the roller coaster started.
ex.zh: 雲霄飛車一開動，他的逞強就消失得無影無蹤。

root.note: 假裝勇敢 → 虛張聲勢

senses.en: used to express approval of a performer

ex.en: The audience stood up and shouted "Bravo!" at the end of the opera.
ex.zh: 歌劇結束時，觀眾起立高喊「太棒了！」

parts.m: brave, excellent 勇敢、傑出（義大利文）

senses.en: (of a donkey) to make a loud, harsh cry
to laugh or speak loudly and harshly

ex.en: We could hear the donkey bray from across the field.
ex.zh: 我們在田野另一邊都聽得到驢子的叫聲。

senses.en: to join metal pieces using melted brass or another alloy

ex.en: The mechanic will braze the broken pipe instead of replacing it.
ex.zh: 技師會用銅焊把斷掉的管子接起來，而不是換新的。

senses.en: a metal container holding burning coals for heat or cooking

ex.en: The guards warmed their hands over a glowing brazier.
ex.zh: 守衛們在燒得通紅的火盆上烤手取暖。

senses.en: an act of breaking a law, rule, or agreement
a gap or break in a wall or barrier
to break through or break a rule

ex.en: Sharing the secret documents was a serious breach of trust.
ex.zh: 洩漏機密文件是嚴重的背信行為。

mn: breach（違反、缺口）和 breech（臀部、槍膛）發音相同，別搞混。

senses.en: a large wave that breaks into white foam on the shore
a person or device that breaks something

ex.en: Surfers waited for the next big breaker to roll in.
ex.zh: 衝浪客等待下一道大浪打過來。

senses.en: the back part of a gun barrel
(old use) the buttocks; a breech birth is a baby born feet or bottom first

ex.en: The soldier loaded a shell into the breech of the cannon.
ex.zh: 士兵把砲彈裝進大砲的砲尾。

senses.en: (old or formal plural of brother) fellow members of a group or religion

ex.en: The farmers stood with their brethren in the neighboring towns.
ex.zh: 農民們與鄰近城鎮的同胞站在一起。

senses.en: the use of few words; conciseness
shortness of time

ex.en: The speech was praised for its brevity and clarity.
ex.zh: 這場演講以簡潔清楚而受到讚賞。

root.note: 短的性質 → 簡潔、短暫

mn: 莎士比亞名言：Brevity is the soul of wit.（簡潔是智慧的靈魂。）

senses.en: small decorative objects of little value

ex.en: Her shelves were crowded with bric-a-brac from her travels.
ex.zh: 她的架子上擺滿了旅行帶回來的小擺設。

root.note: 隨便湊來的小東西 → 小擺設

senses.en: the straps on a horse's head used to control it
to show sudden anger or offense
to bring under control

ex.en: She put the bridle on the horse before the ride.
ex.zh: 騎馬前，她先幫馬套上馬勒。

senses.en: a large military unit made up of several battalions
a group of people organized for a purpose

ex.en: The fire brigade arrived within minutes of the call.
ex.zh: 消防隊接到電話後幾分鐘內就趕到了。

senses.en: a military officer who commands a brigade

ex.en: The brigadier inspected the troops before the parade.
ex.zh: 准將在閱兵前檢閱部隊。

root.note: 指揮一個旅的人 → 旅長

senses.en: a member of a gang that robs travelers in forests or mountains

ex.en: Travelers feared being robbed by a brigand on the mountain pass.
ex.zh: 旅人們害怕在山口遭到土匪搶劫。

senses.en: (old use) sulfur

ex.en: The preacher warned of fire and brimstone for those who sinned.
ex.zh: 傳道人警告犯罪的人將遭受烈火與硫磺的懲罰。

root.note: 會燃燒的石頭 → 硫磺

mn: fire and brimstone 常用來形容「地獄般的懲罰」或激烈的說教。

senses.en: water with a lot of salt in it, used for preserving food
(literary) the sea

ex.en: Soak the cucumbers in brine for a week to make pickles.
ex.zh: 把小黃瓜泡在鹽水裡一週就能做成醃黃瓜。
